units: <cite ref="Nedarim 4b:5">Ned. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>משום דלא אית ליה ק׳</he> because there is no definite term for it (a vow of abstinence, unless explicitly limited, is for ever); <he>אבל … דאית ליה ק׳ וכ׳</he> but as to a Nazarite’s vow where there is a definite term (a Nazarite’s vow, unless qualified, being for thirty days) &c. Ib. 86ᵃ <he>התם קיץ אשה … ק׳</he> there (in the case of the transfer of a field for ten years) there is a definite end stipulated, but can a woman (dedicating her handiwork to the sanctuary after she shall be divorced) define the time? <cite ref="Bava Metzia 67b:4">B. Mets. 67ᵇ</cite> <he>בק׳</he> by definite stipulation of the time up to which the mortgagee may have the privilege of usufruct.

<cite ref="Ketubot 54b:8">Keth. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>מהו דתימא קַיְיצוּתָא עבדו וכ׳</he> you may have thought that the Rabbis instituted a definite sum as the wife’s jointure in order not to put the poor to shame. Y. ib. VI, 30ᵈ top (in Hebr. dict.) <he>אם עשת ק׳</he> if she had a stipulation to that effect made (in her marriage contract); <cite ref="Tosefta Ketubot 6:6">Tosef. ib. VI, 6</cite> <he>קִיצָתָהּ</he>, v. <cite ref="S01125"><he>קִיצָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shevuot 42a:1">Shebu. 42ᵃ</cite> <he>קי׳ דתרעא וכ׳</he> Ms. F. (ed. <he>קצ׳</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 8) stipulations of prices one is likely to remember well.—V. <cite ref="S01821"><he>קְצִיצָה</he></cite>.
